text:
Sam: FYI saw a burst from tenant acme that produced a bunch of 413/429s to the embeddings endpoint this morning. looks like client started compressing vectors and our preflight rejected the framing.
Jia: ugh, do we have the raw request sample/logs? request size or header?
Sam: pasted the failing curl they sent, and the runtime error: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \
  -d @payload.gz
```
runtime log: `ingress: payload-frame invalid: compressed=true but framing=none -> reject (413)`
Leo: interesting — they used gzip so bytes were small but we rejected because our preflight only inspects uncompressed size. we treat Content-Encoding as passthrough right now.
Avery: why are we rejecting instead of decompressing at edge? decompressing costs CPU and changes our unit accounting.
Sam: exactly. decompressing then counting units vs counting compressed bytes gives different billing and quota semantics. acme expects smaller network cost but we still pay CPU.
Jia: for the product side we need deterministic units. currently quota is "embedding-units" (n vectors * length buckets). switching to bytes would break a bunch of customers.
Leo: proposal: add an explicit compression-handshake header so clients advertise compressed payloads and their original vector count/avg-len. e.g. `X-Embed-Client-Meta: vectors=120;avg_len=1024;encoding=gzip`
Avery: that feels safer than guessing. then runtime can choose: 1) accept and decompress on ingest and bill on uncompressed units, 2) reject and ask client to send uncompressed, or 3) fast-path: if encoding supported and tenant has burst-credit flag, accept compressed and bill by bytes with a visible note.
Sam: +1 for a tenant-level burst-credit flag. acme has predictable bursts and would trade CPU for lower egress.
Jia: we also need telemetry: show compressed_ratio, cpu_uncompress_secs, bytes_in vs units_charged. console should expose these so customers understand the delta.
Leo: implementation note — routing affinity matters. if we decompress at edge then we lose KV-cache locality for subsequent autoregressive calls unless we route to same worker. Suggest adding `affinity-key` header so we can keep the tenant on same pool for short TTL.
Avery: also need a safe rollout: start with a canary for tenants opted-in (beta feature) and a dashboard card that surfaces any unit accounting changes. maybe show a diff metric: `billed_units_post_decompression - billed_units_pre_decompression`.
ingest-bot: alert: tenant=acme alert_type=embed-reject-rate threshold=5% window=5m current=12%
Jia: ok action items: (1) API: add optional `X-Embed-Client-Meta` and `affinity-key` headers, (2) runtime: support `Content-Encoding: gzip` with configurable tenant policy (reject/decompress/bytes-bill), (3) billing: define mapping for bytes->embedding-units for backward compatibility, (4) console: add compression telemetry and a diff card for canary tenants.
Leo: I'll sketch a runtime patch for the decompress toggle and affinity routing this week.
Sam: I'll create an eng-platform ticket with the payload sample and link to the billing doc.
Avery: I'll wire a small console mockup for the compression metrics (compressed_ratio, extra_cpu_ms, billed_unit_delta).
ops-bot: suggested rollout policy: canary=5% tenants -> 25% -> full in 3 weeks, monitor: error-rate, billed-delta, cpu-usage.
Jia: thanks. if someone from billing/product can chime in on the mapping soon that'd unblock the canary. otherwise we'll start with opt-in beta. :thumbsup:
